name: Red air: heavy multirotor bomber (G2)
description: Baba Yaga class agricultural conversion. Night bombing from 5-12 km standoff; drops several munitions and returns.

maxTurnRateDegS.note: Planning factor: the flight-path turn rate a multirotor can hold at its cruise speed is g tan(tilt) / V. No tilt limit is published for the Vampire or R18 class; the PX4 MPC_MAN_TILT_MAX default of 35° is used for a loaded heavy multirotor. At the record's cruise speed 12 m/s: 6.9 / 12 rad/s = 33°/s. The body yaw-rate cap (DJI publishes 100 to 300°/s; PX4 MC_YAWRATE_MAX 200°/s) is not a path turn limit and is not used.

climbRateMps.note: Planning factor: no climb rate is published for the Vampire or R18 (Army Recognition and Kyiv Post give 80 km/h top speed, 15 kg payload, 400 m operating altitude). The PX4 MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP default of 3.0 m/s is used for a loaded heavy multirotor.

maxAccelMps2.note: Planning factor: a multirotor's horizontal acceleration is g tan(tilt). No tilt limit is published; the PX4 MPC_MAN_TILT_MAX default of 35° is used for a loaded heavy multirotor. 9.81 × tan 35° = 6.9 m/s².

radiatedPowerW.note: Planning factor: No Vampire or R18 source publishes no link power. The class flies on 700 to 900 MHz UHF control through airborne or marine repeaters (Defence Express; Kyiv Post). The only OEM-published link power in this threat set is Mugin's SprintLink family (2 W, 5 W, 10 W at 1.4 GHz for 30 to 150 km); the 2 W entry-level class is used for a small-UAS command and video link.

attributes.emissionsNote: Custom links, often 700-900 MHz with repeater
attributes.rangeNote: Night sorties 10-20 km with ~15 kg payload; Starlink-relay control reported on some airframes.

linkProtocol.source: Defence Express (radio control in the 700 to 900 MHz band through a marine-drone repeater) and Kyiv Post (mothership signal repeater, Starlink control on some)
linkProtocol.note: Custom UHF control links, not a named COTS protocol.
